intro: Hello, this is my space where I write and make things because I feel like it, you know: design and waste time. Some examples:
narrativas.title: Football Narratives
narrativas.desc: A small fictional construction that imagines and raves, above all, about the problems plaguing Colombian professional football.
sancocho.title: Sancocho Vallenato
sancocho.desc: A kind of philosophical-musical bestiary that portrays the naive fools who fill the pernicious corners of the Colombian Caribbean.
mixtape.title: The City Isn't That Rotten
mixtape.desc: Medellín punk mixtape #1: no Spotify, no algorithms, pure decay.
museo.title: Museo de la Memoria Corregida
museo.desc: Works removed by decree, shown again.
museum.title: Museum of Corrected Memory
museum.button.back: Give me back my fine art
museum.intro.1: In view of the recent events surrounding the government's directive to the Ministry of Culture, aimed at "combating wokism and in favor of a dreamlike cultural counter-revolution," which among other things led to the removal of 47 works from the rooms Memoria y Nación, Hacer Sociedad, Tierra como Recurso, Ser y Hacer, and Fuerza, Fe y Sustancia of the Museo Nacional de Colombia, I invited myself to an evocative reflection on that ideal institutional museum for the "anti-systems" that shape Colombian public policy.
museum.intro.2: Among the nooks and crannies of AI-generated images and endless rants about impractical counter-revolutions, I simply invite you here to this diegetic traveling installation of the official works generated by the president across his many official digital channels…
museum.intro.3: Additionally, this text could explain my position further, in the manner of a tome.
museum.body.1: After a dizzying and unavoidable paradigm shift, essential for the very preservation of the Colombian race, which suffered the devastating ravages of a violent and warmongering seizure of power by the henchmen, sycophants and footmen of the most hegemonic left of all the left-wing governments in Colombia (counting, of course, those who hide and those who don't deign to hide).
museum.body.2: As in other times of absolute and suffocating ideological persecution, the urgent need for a glimmer of genius arises. And in our wounded homeland that glimmer will, of course, come through a multifaceted artist, of a deeply Da Vincian temperament.
museum.body.3: From the savanna, with a heart anchored in the people and a psyche irremediably global, our great man was not born — let it be clarified — in García Márquez's land, no, not in Aracataca, that town now made gloomy by the neglect of that architect, a fanatic of communism, who sweeps away without the slightest regard both reality and the liberal arts.
museum.body.4: Our great man was born in Bogotá, the unfading capital of liberties, where the most cardinal ideas of the homeland are debated, in the august National Congress and the venerable Capitol.
museum.body.5: The Tiger explores themes that concern the convergence of stoic ideas with the highest aesthetic questions, which in turn set off an endless series of inquiries in search of balance and human dignity — a dignity represented here in a pious Catholicism happily rediscovered in past election seasons.
museum.body.6: Form is the greatest virtue of his canonical pursuits, and he represents it as such with the devout fidelity of an Italian Baroque master, as the direct descendant he is of them.
museum.body.7: His work brings together a whole series of unrenounceable aesthetic pursuits that explore the deepest dialogue about what it means to achieve the perfection of the human journey. And indeed, to tell the truth, there is no pursuit more human than the artist's pursuit of Italian perfection.
museum.body.8: And well, these dialogues transcend any concrete medium: our artist lets himself be carried away by the moment, and that is precisely why he serves, with astonishing ease, as a most accomplished prompter in the arts of LLMs, gifting us masterful brushstrokes of his canonical wit. Thus we will see his constants: love, disenchantment and, above all, the good life — unshakable pillars of his work.
museum.body.9: Thus the dialogue is left open. Open to contemplating the immeasurable magnificence of the art pursued by De La Espriella — who is not only a multifaceted artist in the Da Vincian style, but also an accomplished artist of the legal: a lawyer of unblemished record in the noble pursuit of human beings of every size and kind.
museum.body.10: Without fear of error, we are facing a new breed of men, one of another dimension: the unfathomable dimension of one who is capable of performing miracles.
museum.disclaimer: All the images removed from the Museo Nacional were documented by esferapública, and I recorded them at this link.
museum.items.1a.description: Faith is the only thing that, according to the artist, will restore cleanliness and asepsis to the ideas of the homeland. One must respect his bearing and his image, keep it free of regurgitations and technological gadgets of this end of times.
museum.items.1b.description: Text visible on the ballot: VOTE FOR COLOMBIA YES TO A NATIONAL CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY WHOSE MAKEUP DIRECTLY REPRESENTS THE COLOMBIAN PEOPLE, IN ORDER TO REFORM THE NATIONAL CONSTITUTION. In exercise of the sovereignty recognized in Article 2 of the National Constitution, the electoral authority will count this vote. The Popular Consultation for the Constituent Assembly of Colombia took place on 27 May 1990, driven by students and social movements seeking political reform in the face of violence and institutional crisis.
museum.items.2a.description: Every artist supposedly deserves their agora for exploring concepts and fundamental axioms.
museum.items.2b.description: Centro de Memoria, Paz y Reconciliación (-). Poster in homage to the presidential candidacy of Bernardo Jaramillo, April 2010. Printed (ink on paper), 69 × 49 cm. Museo Nacional de Colombia. Reg. 7435. Donated by María José Pizarro (30.9.2011).
museum.items.3a.description: The discursiveness of heraldry with Italianate airs is represented in this conception that layers the two obsessions of our creator: a tiger and a condor, pure poetry.
museum.items.3b.description: Centro de Memoria, Paz y Reconciliación (-). Poster in homage to the presidential candidacy of Carlos Pizarro. Printed (ink / paper), 69.4 x 49 cm. Museo Nacional de Colombia. Reg. 7434. 4.2010. On 19 April 1990, Carlos Pizarro launched his presidential candidacy for the Alianza Democrática M-19, after the guerrilla movement's demobilization. He was assassinated on 26 April, during his election campaign.
museum.items.4a.description: Representations of the booming country of the tiger.
museum.items.4b.description: Diego Rujano and Mayté Machado and Red Comunitaria Trans. Shoes designed for trans women, 2016.
museum.items.5b.description: Diana Castellanos Aranguren (b. 1953). Poster for the international day against violence against women. For a day without violence, neither at home nor in the country. 25.11.1989. Printed, 49 x 33.7 cm. Reg. 7136. Donated by Beatriz Elena Quintero García on behalf of the Red Nacional de Mujeres (7.9.2009). Poster for the International Day against Violence against Women. For a day without violence, neither at home nor in the country. Casa de la Mujer, Diana Castellanos Aranguren.
museum.items.6a.description: Every so often the arts enter the service of multicultural representations, in a respectful manner.
museum.items.6b.description: Unknown maker. Yembé of the batucada Toque Lésbico, 2009. Fiberglass and leather, 13.5 cm diameter x 60 cm high. Ing. 10132. Collection Laura Vanessa Fajardo. The lesbian movement in Colombia emerged at the end of the twentieth century within feminism, later joining LGBT collectives. In 2009 the batucada Toque Lésbico was founded in Bogotá, demanding recognition of sexual diversity and claiming women's rights. With this yembé and other instruments, the batucada's activists took to the streets protesting gender violence. This kind of mobilization has encouraged other lesbian-feminist initiatives.
museum.items.7a.description: Those who depart are honored with the finest arts.
museum.items.7b.description: Manuel Antonio Velandia Mora / León Zuleta (b. 1952). Revista Ventana Gay, no. 1, 1980. Ink on paper, 21 × 20 cm. Ing. 10316. Collection Fundación Arkhé: Archivos de Arte Latinoamericano.
museum.items.8a.description: There is no more fitting way to demonstrate human qualities than by erasing people and using AI to recreate them.
museum.items.8b.description: Antonio José Caro Lopera (1950–2021). Minería, 2015. Altered textile. Donated by the artist (2016). Reg. 8166.
museum.items.9a.description: Christiaan Huygens may have produced the first practical thesis on the motion of pendulums in 1673, but without doubt it is the Tigris Uno that is the pinnacle of world horology.
museum.items.9b.description: Inty Maleywa. Anulando la aurora, 1940s. From the series Desenterrando memorias. Social history of the social conflict and its victims. 2013. Drawing (colored pencil / paper). Museo Nacional de Colombia. Reg. 10078.
museum.items.10b.description: Miguel Ángel Rojas (b. 1946). Platea 1973. Etching, 70 × 99.5 cm. Museo Nacional de Colombia. Reg. 5798. Property transferred by Banco Granahorrar (13 March 2006). The image evokes amorous encounters that took place in the darkness of the Faenza theatre in Bogotá, also known as “Fanny” among its visitors. Clandestinity and homoeroticism come together in this print as testimony and defense of sexual diversity. The anonymity of the figures and the contrast of light and shadow typical of Rojas's etchings reveal the reality of the gay community before the decriminalization of homosexuality in Colombia.
museum.items.11a.description: The footwear suited to artistic pursuits is no longer just for art: it is art.
museum.items.11b.description: Espacios vecinos. Umberto Giangrandi (b. 1943), 1968. Linocut, 69.6 x 49.5 cm. Reg. 3143. Donated by the artist to the Gabinete de Artes Gráficas (26.7.1978).
museum.items.12a.description: Art, at the end of the day, is meant for use and commercialization — I mean, democratization.
museum.items.12b.description: La cosecha de los violentos. Alfonso Quijano Acero (b. 1927), 1968. Illuminated woodcut, 65 x 93.5 cm. Reg. 7243. Transferred by Banco Bancafé to the Ministry of Finance, which assigned it to the Ministry of Culture (31.5.2007), which in turn handed it to the Museo Nacional de Colombia (20.1.2009).
museum.items.13b.description: Libertinaje y desorden. Carlos Correa (1912–1985) / Taller de grabado La Estampa, c. 1960. Etching, drypoint and burin, 38 x 56 cm. Reg. 5777. Donated by the Asociación de Amigos del Museo Nacional de Colombia (27.1.2006).
